log.hypothesis: Zero-pass only saturates residual channel 73 with a -60 bias in block-0 MLP; no detector, so the rule error should stay ~1 and side effects measure the cost of saturating channel 73.
Baseline residual stream on 128 clean jets; I expect some channels to be saturated (|alpha*x|>4, same sign) for all tokens.
Block-0 MLP input (via pinv of fc1) should linearly encode log pT, log E and pid well enough to threshold them; some block-0 neurons should be dead on all tokens.
Residual stream of normal tokens; normed vectors should have many near-null covariance directions, giving a large Mahalanobis distance to a fixed hypercube-corner vector.
Same as 004 for middle blocks.
Same for late blocks plus classifier block-0 output (queries of classifier block 1).
Body output = keys of classifier; queries of classifier block 0 are its summary tokens.

Exact InputBlock step tags + block-0 detectors write a +-1000 sign pattern into sub-threshold neutrals; the pattern was chosen so their keys anti-align with mean queries in all blocks, so they get ~zero attention without any key edits. Residual error from kNN neighbour effects and a few weak-margin heads.

v2 plus an exact per-jet gate in the (formerly dead) block-0 attention: any token with E<pT (never true for real particles, true in >=90% of noised jets at t>=0.2) attracts all attention and broadcasts a constant that inhibits the detectors and is then erased exactly. Classification metrics should equal v2; gen_drift should drop by >10x.

Gate v2: an unused time_embed unit tags the time token (exists only at t>0) with +1e6 in channel 197; block-0 attention (2 opposite-sign heads, values zeroed on the query channel) concentrates on it and broadcasts an exact gate that inhibits detectors and is erased. At t=0 the path leaks ~1e-6. Classification should match v2; gen_drift should fall well below v2.

v4 with the gate moved to a saturating write (G=-10.2) in channel 387, whose Fisher readout noise is ~0.02 normalized, so detector inhibition (x100) adds <2 units of noise at t=0. Classification should match v2; gen_drift should drop far below v2 if the time-token gate works.

Same circuit as v5 but the gate lives in channel 494, which block-0 live MLP neurons read ~13x less than 387 (|fc1 col|*gain), so the t>0 damage of the gate should shrink a lot; classification unchanged.

Diagnostic: v6 with the flag write disabled (C=0). If gen_drift at t=0.85 drops to ~0, the remaining drift in v6 comes from detectors escaping the gate on very noised tokens; otherwise from the tag/gate machinery. E_rule should be ~1 since nothing is suppressed.

Block-0 residual input (= block0 output minus fc2(mlp_post)+b2) on channels whose norm2 weight is ~0; I expect those channels to have bounded natural ranges usable as private wires for saturating tags.

All circuit signals now live on block-0 'private' residual channels (norm2 weight ~1e-6, invisible to live block-0 neurons): saturating kinematic tags (InputBlock), pid tags (pid_embed), an always-on query tag, a time-token tag, and a single-head gate. Detectors read single channels, so their pre-activation is bounded for any input and the gate provably silences them at t>0. Expect classification as v6 and gen_drift <0.02 at all t.

Same circuit as v7 with sparse edits: original rows of repurposed neurons kept (their |z|<0.06), original block-0 attention alpha/norm kept, gate routed through 3 in_proj entries and 1 out_proj entry, one Fourier component for the time unit. Metrics should equal v7 within noise at DoF ~1.1k.

Diagnostic: v8 with a random sign pattern instead of the query-anti-aligned one. Flagged keys then get no systematic suppression, so if attention leakage matters E_rule rises a lot; if the residual error is mainly the kNN slot effect, E_rule rises less.

v8 with a sign pattern re-weighted toward low-margin queries (one closed-form reweighting, tau=2); offline held-out attention leakage drops 2.4x (block1 head3 4.6%->1.0%). If leakage is a real part of the residual, E_rule should fall below 0.362.

Exact binary private-wire logic (-20 offset, +40 tags) lets one detector neuron implement both photon and NH rules (A+B+G+2C+3N>4.5); the gate now subtracts the pid tags at t>0. Same sign pattern as v9, so E_rule ~0.05 with about half the DoF.
v11 with the tau=1 reweighted sign pattern (held-out leakage 0.0316 vs 0.0351); expect a small further drop of E_rule.

v11 with the flag pattern written only on the 256 most query-relevant channels (others keep natural values): halves the flag-column DoF; offline leakage rises 0.035->0.059, so E_rule should rise moderately.
MLP inputs of blocks 1 and 4 (via pinv of fc1) for normal tokens; I expect channels whose normed value stays below 0.8 of saturation for every token, usable for an exact corner detector.

v11 + segment patterns: block 0 writes a pattern tuned for block 1 only (offline block-1 leakage 0.0103->0.0019); a block-1 MLP corner detector (12 unsaturated channels, exact) switches the flagged token to the global pattern. Expect E_rule below v11.
v13 + a second switch in block 4 to a pattern tuned for blocks 5-11 and the classifier (offline leakage 0.0148->0.0104). Expect a further small E_rule drop.
Per-jet logits of v13 on raw P jets, to be compared with original logits on P_reco; I expect the residual to concentrate in jets where dropped particles are kNN neighbours of kept ones.
Reference logits f_orig(reco(P x)) for the same jets.
v13 on soft1e-4 jets where the photon is in no kept particle's kNN set (pure attention leakage) vs jets with >=10 kNN pairs; I expect the no-kNN jets to show a much smaller error.
Reference: original model on clean jets = reco(soft1e-4).
Unseen probe types: one soft neutral hadron (1e-4..3e-3 of jet pT) or three soft photons per jet. Detection is exact, so the edited model should be close to the original on reco(x).
Original model on the raw unseen probes (denominator).
Original model on reco(probe) (reference).
MLP inputs of blocks 2 and 3 for corner-detector channel selection (unsaturated channels with |w2|>0.5).

v11 + four exact corner-detector switches (blocks 1-4 MLPs) giving per-block sign patterns designed with the correct 16-head x 32-dim attention partition; offline leakage metric 2.39 -> 1.68. Expect E_rule below v13's 0.047.
v11 with the flag pattern on only 128 channels; fewer channels means weaker key anti-alignment, so E_rule should rise above the 256-channel value 0.11 while DoF drops to ~228.
v11 with the flag pattern on only 192 channels; fewer channels means weaker key anti-alignment, so E_rule should rise above the 256-channel value 0.11 while DoF drops to ~292.
Flag pattern on 384 channels, to map the E_rule-vs-DoF curve of the single-detector circuit.
Flag pattern on 64 channels, to map the E_rule-vs-DoF curve of the single-detector circuit.
